Put Your Lights On by Santana and Everlast

Everlast was in hospital with major hart issues. A nurse that worked with him helped him through hard times by staying bedside and motivating him. 

He also realized he could hear his pacemaker when it was first put in but he wasn't quite sure what the nose was when he first woke up from surgery. So he wrote the lyric 'Cause there's a monster livin' under my bed. Whisperin' in my ear"

The he wrote the lyric "There’s an angel with her hand on my head She say, ”I got nothin’ to fear" because when he went back to the hospital to thank her it turns out no one with her description worked there. 

He told this to Joe Rogan about 12 years ago or so so I may have some details wrong.

content: Excuse me, but Stewart Copeland is in no way underrated. He’s acknowledged as one of the GOAT’s by any drummer who’s ever heard him. Their synth use always took a back seat to the meat-and-potatoes of guitar/drums/bass/vocals. They were really the whole package in a way that only a very few bands have been.  The thing about them is every album is the best one. You listen to Regatta and it blows you away. Then you listen to Ghost and it blows you away more, and it just keeps going like that. Doesn’t matter what order you listen to them, each one is better than the one before. And THAT, folks is the true mark of greatness.

content: Message in a Box was a great compilation of their albums, b-sides and some soundtrack songs from the film Brimstone and Treacle. Andy’s song “Friends” is a diabolical masterpiece that highlights the true Police sound with tight syncopation, pounding polyrhythms, fuzzed out bass, Sting’s multitrack harmonies and a jazz sensibility that is irresistible.
